London, 1<sup>st</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**President Barack Obama** believes a quick, negotiated bankruptcy is the most likely way for GM to restructure and become a competitive automaker, people familiar with the matter said. Obama said GM’s and Chrysler’s recovery plans were insufficient. He gave GM 60 days to come up with deeper cost and debt reductions than the biggest U.S. automaker proposed in its plan submitted last month.  He said he would consider more aid for Chrysler only if it completed a partnership with Fiat within 30 days. 

GM must shrink $27.5 billion in debt that bondholders have been reluctant to exchange for equity and $20.4 billion in obligations to a union-run health-care fund. A bankruptcy may make recoveries for bondholders and the UAW more difficult. “We’ll get it done in court or we’ll get it done out of court,” said new CEO Henderson. Creditors doubt an equity exchange can be completed by the 60-day deadline. 

The government probably is considering putting GM and Chrysler into bankruptcy and then quickly selling their best assets to form new companies, said Rod Lache, a Deutsche Bank analyst. GM has a contingency plan ready for a new company that would split off its best assets into an entity that might later be sold.  The process, a “363 sale” that refers to a section of bankruptcy code, would be a way to keep the automakers from sitting in a prolonged bankruptcy that might undermine sales of their vehicles.  “The administration is a bit more focused on a structured, or prepackaged, bankruptcy than some might think,” Representative Candice Miller said. Stakes of any dissident creditors, including bondholders, would be “crammed down” or forcibly reduced in a bankruptcy. 

The new GM would be powered by brands such as Cadillac and Chevrolet and valuable foreign operations. Unprofitable brands, such as Hummer, would be hived off in bankruptcy court.   While the new company could be created in 30 days or less, bankruptcy may go on much longer, focused on bad assets. Senator Carl Levin said the public focus on a bankruptcy risks bringing about that very scenario. An auto bankruptcy may push production low enough to wipe four percentage points from U.S. gross domestic product in a single quarter, Jim Reid of Deutsche Bank said. One-third of the three million people employed in the industry could lose their jobs. The bank’s price target for GM is zero. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Honda** said on Tuesday it would cut production in North America by 62,000 vehicles by shutting factories for 13 days starting in May and reduce pay for salaried and factory workers. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Wesizwe Platinum** has signed a term sheet with YA Global Investments for a three-year standby equity distribution facility worth R550-million.  The private equity firm would subscribe for up to R550million worth of ordinary shares in Wesizwe, in minimum tranches of R50-million.  Wesizwe confirmed that it wou

ld still proceed with its flagship Frischgewaagd-Ledig on a phased basis.  The project has been modularised into a series of smaller components each with separate budgets and contracts.  The 12 phases of the project will be comissioned between 2013 and 2014, and the remaining phases between 2016 and 2017.  Wesizwe made a net loss of R27,8-million in 08, vs. R90,8-million in 07. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Palladium** , in the last ten days of March, showed a surprisingly positive move for these troubled times. The white metal rose till last Thursday, partly driven by hopes for a trend change in automobile sales in the USA, to $227/oz.  It thus breached its high from middle February but was still quite a way from its early November high of $235/oz. While speculative buying last week certainly came mainly from American participants, dealers also reported Japanese buying. In the end, the metal could not hold onto all its gains and lost ground hitting $ 214/oz again. _Source: Heraeus Precious Metals Weekly_
